MindView

MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence

Language-guided target-view generation from multiple RGB images of indoor scenes.

Yanbo Wang1, Yihao Liu2, Jiwen Lu3

1 MindView project  ·  2 Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory  ·  3 Department of Automation, Tsinghua University

Overview

MindView evaluates whether a generative model can observe several views of an indoor scene, understand a spatial query, and render the requested target view. The benchmark contains 1,500 cases from 513 scenes across ScanNet, ScanNet++, and ARKitScenes. The standard input is six context images and one spatial query; target images, depth, and numerical camera parameters are withheld from the generator.

The release combines the benchmark, a reproducible BAGEL supervised fine-tuning recipe, a published BAGEL-SFT checkpoint, and spatial-understanding transfer evaluations. Nested C3/C6/C10 settings create 4,500 experiment records over the same frozen cases.

1,500benchmark cases
513indoor scenes
7spatial tasks
6primary metrics

Benchmark protocol

Each frozen record couples ordered RGB context views with a language instruction. A model receives only the context images and query, then produces one 512 × 512 RGB image. The fixed target and ten-view geometry references are used only by the evaluation pipeline.

StageGenerator accessEvaluator-only information
ContextSix ordered RGB views of the same indoor scene.Fixed target view and ten geometry-scoring references.
InstructionOne language query describing a spatial change or object relation.Depth and numerical camera parameters.
PredictionOne 512 × 512 RGB target-view image.Reference images and metric computation.

Table 1. Information available to the generator and retained by the evaluation pipeline.

Task taxonomy

Seven tasks probe camera motion, object-centered intent, and instructions that combine both forms of spatial evidence.

Geometry-dominant tasks

  1. 01
    TranslationMove to a requested position.
  2. 02
    RotationTurn the viewpoint toward a new direction.
  3. 03
    CompositionChange position and orientation together.

Semantics-dominant tasks

  1. 04
    Relational object groundingLocate an object through relations to its surroundings.
  2. 05
    Target-facing reorientationReorient the camera toward a named target.
  3. 06
    Object-centric repositioningMove around an object while preserving its role.
  4. 07
    Multi-cue viewpoint inferenceResolve several spatial cues in one instruction.

Evaluation

MindView reports six primary components across visual alignment, semantic consistency, image quality, and geometry. Scores are aggregated by task before the overall average; CLIP-I is retained as an auxiliary comparison.

MetricEvaluation focusRole
DINO-IImage-level visual alignmentPrimary
SemanticObject and instruction consistencyPrimary
SpatialViewpoint and scene arrangementPrimary
QualityPerceptual image qualityPrimary
VGGT-RScoreRelative geometric structurePrimary
VGGT-TScoreTranslation consistencyPrimary
CLIP-IAuxiliary image similarityAuxiliary

Table 2. Primary and auxiliary components in the public evaluation chain.

Release

The public repository contains the evaluation pipeline, frozen metadata, BAGEL-SFT recipe, inference code, and transfer evaluation guides. The linked Hugging Face repositories provide the benchmark, training data, and inference checkpoint.
